rationale:
Evidence: iteration 8 (sensor x narrowed to -0.03..0.03, y 0.06, sensor_size 0.012, kp 4.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.30, base_speed 1.3) is the best raced design at 116.27, up from 93.70. The narrower spread lifted progress on every track (oval 0.41 to 0.46, s-bend 0.17 to 0.26, slalom 0.10 to 0.12). The Evaluator's 93.70 return rule was written before the race, so only its oscillation clause still applies. Oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.262, above the 0.25 threshold, and s-bend reached 0.255. Line-loss events also rose (oval 1.25, slalom 1.7). max_error is still 0.0637 to 0.0655 m on every track, so the off-track floor has not moved.

Change: keep the iteration 8 geometry (x -0.03..0.03, y 0.06, sensor_size 0.012), because it is the source of the score gain. Lower kp from 4.0 to 3.7 to bring oscillation back under 0.25. Across iterations 1 to 4, kp increases consistently raised oscillation (kp 3.0 at kd 0.15 gave 0.164 on the oval, kp 4.0 at kd 0.20 gave 0.208). kd, ki, base_speed, weights and line_loss are unchanged.

Hypotheses: (1) a modest kp reduction keeps oval oscillation under about 0.25 while progress stays near the 0.46 level; (2) the narrow array's gain in progress comes from the sensor spread, not from kp. Expected result: oval oscillation about 0.23 to 0.25, score at or above about 110. Risk: lower kp may reduce progress on bends and lower the score. If the score falls below 116.27 with oscillation under 0.25, the next step is to restore kp 4.0 and test a narrower spread (x -0.02..0.02) at kd 0.30.

Measurements wanted: steering_oscillation on every track, progress, line_loss_events, max_error, rms_error, and control_effort. Keep base_speed at 1.3 until progress nears 0.995 with no line loss. Completion within 3 s is not expected at this speed.
